title: Zero query cost
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let a node finder for $k$-juntas on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube be given, let $f$ be a Boolean function on that cube taking values in $\{\pm1\}$, and fix a learning parameter $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$. For every fuel, set $P$ of fixed coordinates, assignment of signs on $P$, and outcome in the support of the recursive learner's output-and-cost distribution, the number of membership queries charged to that outcome is zero.
hypotheses_covered: a node finder for dimension $n$ and junta size $k$
a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$P$ is a set of coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$
the outcome lies in the support of the learner's output-and-cost distribution
